newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds cracked a string of resistance levels to close sharply up on Thursday, just an inch beneath their new record high at 110.67.
"We're not seeing a high volume of trade in cash. Tomorrow we could have same kind of consolidation," a dealer said. "But I guess any level below 110 would be considered a good buy."

Positive news on the Spanish economy and its likely entry into EMU from the start, sparked a bull run. Lower-than-expected October CPI led to an official forecast that inflation might end year below 3.4 pct.
And that could trigger another rate cut, analysts said.
Foreign markets also lent support to bonos, especially after Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he welcomed the dollar's recent improvement.
The 10-year spread over Bunds hit an all-time record at 143 basis points and closed at 145 bps, below the key 150 level.
The three-year 7.80 percent bond ended around 103.84 versus 103.55, yielding 6.31 percent.
"At this point we have a very strange yield curve. I expect either a reduction at the shorter end or a decline in the 10-year segment," a dealer said.
